title: Prompt truncation helper can return strings longer than the requested cap

finding.claim: Prompt truncation helper can return strings longer than the requested cap
finding.recommendation: Reserve space for the truncation marker before slicing, so the final returned string length never exceeds `cap`. For example, compute the marker first, reduce the visible prefix budget by `len(marker)`, and then apply the boundary logic within that reduced budget.

code_region.text:
# ------------------------------------------------- grounding (v0.9.3, §2b)

def _quote_grounded(quote, text):
    """Deterministic grounding check: does the finding's evidence
    quote actually appear in the text the reviewer was shown?

    The reviewer is instructed to copy the cited line exactly
    (without the diff's '+' marker — the line's own text is a
    substring of the diff line, so the plain search still hits).
    Tolerances are narrow and honest: surrounding whitespace, a
    '+' the reviewer kept anyway, and whitespace collapsing. A
    paraphrase does NOT ground — that is the point of the check:
    findings asserted against text the seat never received (the
    review-v14 failure mode, where a complete-coverage panel
    miscounted what it was shown) cannot block on assertion alone."""
    q = (quote or "").strip()
    if len(q) < 4 or not text:
        return False
    if q in text:

refutation.reason: The function returns the constructed string directly; the f-string includes the full len(text) value and the opening bracket, so the output length is determined by the slice `cut` plus the fixed marker length, not by the original text length.

probe.summary: `probes/gap_prompt_slice_probe.py`, result `gap-prompt-slice-3f50bf6b3349.txt` — measured at HEAD: | case | len(text) | cap | len(out) | over cap | |---|---|---|---|---| | one over cap | 101 | 100 | 197 | **+97** | | long prose | 1,759 | 300 | 396 | **+96** | | long single word | 5,000 | 300 | 398 | **+98** | | small cap | 2,500 | 50 | 147 | **+97** | | cap 1 | 5 | 1 | 96 | **+95** | Every over-cap input returns more than the cap — up to ~98 chars over, the length of the marker (which carries the full length and a 64-char sha256). The overshoot is bounded by a constant and does not grow with the input. Scope of harm: the helper slices evidence for adjudication/confirmation prompts (display only — stored record text is never cut by it), so the consequence is prompt budgets running ~100 chars over an internal display cap, not record corruption. This is the same helper PT1's hardening touched for the truncation marker itself (packet #7 in the main set); the marker's honesty is deliberate — the open question is only whether the cap contract should absorb it.
